description: Nostr badge bidirectional-binding conformance vectors for packages/shared/src/badges/nostr.ts's verifyNostrBinding (04-plan Phase A4 task A4.3). Direction 1 = profile.alsoKnownAs carries `nostr:npub1…`; Direction 2 = the user's kind-0 (metadata) event content has `alsoKnownAs: string[]` containing profile.did (see apps/expo/src/nostr/publish.ts's module doc for why this is a JSON content field, not a NIP-39 `i` tag). Each case's `kind0` field is exactly what a NostrKind0Fetcher implementation would resolve for that scenario — `null` means 'fetch could not complete' (network/relay unreachable), an object means 'fetch succeeded, here is the parsed content'. Both App and the future web viewer (05-plan V3) replay this exact file against their own IO-injected fetchKind0 wrapper; the single-direction-no-green-check rule (01-spec §7 / 03-spec §3) is the reason this file exists — every case's `expected.state` must never be 'verified' unless BOTH directions actually hold. `npub`/pubkeyHex reuse the exact reference vector apps/expo/__tests__/unit/nostrUserKey.test.ts's npubEncode suite and packages/shared/test/npub.test.ts already pin (REFERENCE_PUBKEY_HEX/REFERENCE_NPUB), so all three suites can never silently drift apart. `did`/`altDid` reuse the same did:key values already established by packages/shared/vectors/profile.json and didkey.json. Consumed by packages/shared/test/nostrBinding.vectors.test.ts.

cases.name: both-directions-verified
cases.reason: profile claims the npub AND the fetched kind-0's content.alsoKnownAs contains profile.did — this is the only shape that may render a green check.

cases.name: profile-claims-npub-but-kind0-missing-did
cases.reason: profile claims the npub (Direction 1 holds) but the fetched kind-0 event's content has no alsoKnownAs entry for profile.did at all — a one-way claim actively caught mid-flight, not a network failure. Must be `declared`, never `verified`.

cases.name: did-mismatch
cases.reason: kind-0 DOES have an alsoKnownAs array, but it names a DIFFERENT did:key than profile.did — same category as the missing-did case (Direction 2 does not hold), proves the check is exact-match, not merely field-presence.

cases.name: kind0-fetch-null
cases.reason: profile claims the npub, but the kind-0 fetch could not complete at all (relay unreachable/timeout) — we genuinely do not know whether Direction 2 holds right now. Must be `stale`, distinct from the `declared` cases above where we DID see a kind-0 that doesn't reciprocate.

cases.name: no-npub-in-profile
cases.reason: profile.alsoKnownAs has no nostr:npub… entry at all — no Nostr binding was ever claimed, so this is not-a-badge rather than an unconfirmed one-way claim. `npub` is the authoritative 'is there even a claim' signal here: it is null, and callers MUST gate rendering on `npub !== null`, not on `state` alone. `state` is still populated (as `declared`, the closest of the four fixed enum values — see badges/nostr.ts's module doc) purely so the return type stays non-nullable; it is not meaningful on its own for this case.
cases.kind0Unreachable: fetchKind0 must never be called for this case — no pubkey to fetch

cases.name: malformed-npub-in-profile
cases.reason: profile.alsoKnownAs carries a nostr:npub1… entry, but it is not valid bech32 (corrupted checksum — last character flipped from 'g' to 'q' vs. the reference npub). Direction 1 cannot even be confirmed, so fetchKind0 is never called; honest result is `declared`, not `stale` (there is no possible 'was verified before' history for a claim that was never validly formed) and not a thrown error (never throws).
cases.kind0Unreachable: fetchKind0 must never be called for this case — npub does not decode to a pubkey
